This question was a clean OLS-fit task that the existing skill/memory already covers well. The slope and intercept matched gold exactly, and the only OfficeQA-specific subtlety (sign formatting, the minus character, rounding to thousandths) was handled correctly.

Checking against my existing memory: I already have a strong note covering "fit OLS to PROJECT/FORECAST" — plain linear fit on RAW level, no log transform, year as untransformed numeric predictor. This question is just a slope/intercept-reporting variant of that same pattern (not even a forecast, just returning the coefficients). Nothing new emerged:

- No new table layout, page-offset, or parsing gotcha.
- The negative intercept is large simply because untransformed calendar years (1929–1942) are far from zero — that's expected and inherent to non-centered OLS, not a pitfall I tripped on.
- Sign formatting (gold uses Unicode minus −, I used ASCII -, verdict still CORRECT) confirms the grader normalizes minus signs, so no action needed there either.

The one micro-fact possibly worth pinning is that OfficeQA OLS questions can ask for raw slope+intercept (not just a forecast), and untransformed-year intercepts are legitimately large-negative. But that's a trivial corollary of the OLS note I already have, and saving it risks bloating memory (already at 96%).

No skill needed.
